Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: artworkSurface
candidates.comment: A supporting material or substrate for a visual artwork. Also called: art substrate, painting surface, canvas type. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Landscape' artworkSurface 'Canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artworkSurface 'Paper'", "VisualArtwork 'Mural' artworkSurface 'Wall'."

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: photos
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: thumbnail
candidates.comment: A smaller, preview image (thumbnail) associated with a creative work, such as an image or video. Also called "preview image", "thumbnail graphic", "miniature image", "small image". Examples: "The video has thumbnail a still frame", "The image gallery's thumbnail is a reduced version", "This creative work displays a thumbnail for quick viewing.". Distinct from image, which refers to the full-size image.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: surface
candidates.comment: An identification of the material used as the surface for a visual artwork. Also called "artwork medium", "painting surface", "material base", "substrate". Examples: "The painting has surface canvas", "The drawing's surface is paper", "This artwork uses a wood surface."

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: exampleOfWork
candidates.comment: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work that it is an instance, realization, or derivation of. Also called: instance of, realization of, derivation of, based on. Examples: "Mona Lisa (print)" example of work "Mona Lisa (original painting)", "Hamlet (film)" example of work "Hamlet (play)", "Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)" example of work "Star Wars: A New Hope (film)".

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: preparation

Also called patient readiness, pre-procedure instructions, pre-op preparation. Examples: A medical procedure requires preparation like 'fasting for 8 hours'. candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

candidates.label: jobImmediateStart
candidates.comment: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer
candidates.comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."

candidates.label: competencyRequired
candidates.comment: A requirement relation for an educational credential or learning resource, specifying the knowledge, skill, or ability needed. Also called "required skill", "prerequisite competency", "learning outcome". Examples: "Certification competencyRequired 'Problem-solving skills'", "Course learning resource competencyRequired 'Basic algebra'".

candidates.label: coursePrerequisites
candidates.comment: A requirement relation between a course and the conditions or prior knowledge needed to take it. Also called: prerequisites, required courses, entry requirements. Examples: "Advanced Algorithms" course prerequisites "Data Structures", "Calculus II" course prerequisites "Calculus I", "Graduate Seminar" course prerequisites "permission of instructor".

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: isUnlabelledFallback

Also called default settings, fallback rule, general application, unlabelled default. Examples: DeliveryTimeSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. ShippingRateSettings has isUnlabelledFallback set to 'true'. These settings are isUnlabelledFallback for all products.

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical restriction relation between a software application and the countries where it is not supported. Also called: unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "App X" countries not supported "Cuba", "Software Y" countries not supported "Iran, North Korea", "Game Z" countries not supported "Syria". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists where the application is supported.

candidates.label: secondaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A preventative therapy or intervention aimed at preventing the recurrence of a medical condition after an initial episode. Also called relapse prevention, post-episode prevention, reoccurrence therapy. Examples: `Heart Attack` secondaryPrevention `Aspirin Therapy`, `Stroke` secondaryPrevention `Lifestyle Modification: Diet and Exercise`, `Depression` secondaryPrevention `Medical Therapy: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy`. Distinct from `primaryPrevention`, which aims to prevent the *initial* occurrence.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: earlyPrepaymentPenalty

Also called "prepayment fee", "early payoff penalty", "exit fee". Examples: "Mortgage repayment earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$500'", "Loan agreement earlyPrepaymentPenalty '2% of remaining balance'", "Car loan earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$100'".

candidates.label: coursePrerequisites
candidates.comment: A requirement relation between a course and the conditions or prior knowledge needed to take it. Also called: prerequisites, required courses, entry requirements. Examples: "Advanced Algorithms" course prerequisites "Data Structures", "Calculus II" course prerequisites "Calculus I", "Graduate Seminar" course prerequisites "permission of instructor".

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: suitableForDiet

Also called "dietary suitability", "dietary compliance", "dietary restriction friendly", "accommodates diet". Examples: "The recipe is suitableForDiet VeganDiet", "The menu item's suitableForDiet is GlutenFreeDiet", "This dish is suitableForDiet HalalDiet."
